title: Parallel / perpendicular slope
subtitle: Linear equations in two variables · 20 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **20 of the official questions in Linear equations in two variables are this one** — 5 Easy, 7 Medium, 8 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Hard tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The words 'perpendicular to' or 'parallel to' appear.
- Line one is given as an equation in standard form, as two points, or as a graph, and you're asked for the slope of line two, or for a point on line two.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Get the slope of the given line: rearrange to y = mx + b (for Ax + By = C, the slope is -A/B), or use rise over run between two points.
- 2) Parallel keeps the same slope; perpendicular flips the fraction and changes the sign.
- 3) If you need a point, build y = mx + b using the given intercept or point and substitute.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Graph the given equation and click two lattice points to read the slope.
You can check a perpendicular answer by graphing it and seeing a right angle, but the negative reciprocal is faster by hand.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The wrong choices include the original slope, its reciprocal without the sign change, and the negative without the reciprocal.
In standard form, you might also read A (or -A) as the slope instead of -A/B.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The wrong choices include the original slope, its reciprocal without the sign change, and the negative without the reciprocal.
In standard form, you might also read A (or -A) as the slope instead of -A/B.
